summary: Dedicated pool throughput degraded after autoscaler threshold change causing GPU contention and client timeouts for BrightWave
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightWave reported elevated tail latency and repeated request timeouts starting ~2026-03-10T08:15Z on their dedicated GPU pool in us-west-2. The problem coincided with an autoscaler parameter change applied in the morning (scale-down threshold decreased from 20% to 5% idle).

Impact:
- BrightWave reported ~30% of inferences timing out (client-side 10s timeout) between 08:15–11:00 UTC.
- End-to-end p95 latency for rw-alpha-7b-v2 increased from ~120ms to ~1.6s; p99 spiked to 6–12s.
- Throughput for the dedicated pool dropped by ~40% compared to baseline.
- Errors observed: intermittent 500s from serving runtime and occasional 503 from gateway when nodes were being evicted.

Environment:
- Customer: BrightWave Analytics (dedicated pool, committed capacity)
- Region: us-west-2 (prod-us-west)
- Pool name: bw-prod-pool-03
- Node types: A100-80GB equivalent, 8 nodes pre-change
- Models: rw-alpha-7b-v2 (primary), rw-alpha-7b-quant (fallback)

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) 2026-03-10 07:58 UTC: Ops applied autoscaler config update (reduce idle threshold, faster scale-down) via infra-config PR (see linked PR).
2) 08:10 UTC: Several node terminations started as pool scaled down to 3 nodes to reduce cost/bursting headroom.
3) 08:15–08:45 UTC: Sudden increase in queuing at gateway; requests from BrightWave began to experience timeouts and elevated latency.
4) 08:30–10:00 UTC: Monitoring shows one or two long-running customer batch jobs (internal ML training job) pinned to shared nodes in same pool; these produced sustained GPU utilization and caused KV-cache pressure and GPU memory fragmentation across remaining serving pods.
5) 09:20 UTC: Support engaged SRE; mitigations attempted: paused scale-down, raised pool size to 6 nodes, evicted noisy job where possible.
6) 10:40 UTC: Throughput restored to within 10% of baseline after evicting noisy-run and increasing pool to 8 nodes; customer confirmed reduced timeouts.

Logs / metrics references (links):
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/bw/pool-bw-prod-pool-03?from=2026-03-10T07:00:00Z&to=2026-03-10T12:00:00Z
- Cloud logs (node-term events): https://logs.redwood.ai/q/bw-prod-pool-03-node-events
- Incident Slack thread: #support (thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C012ABCDEF/p164698)
- Autoscaler PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/realtime-autoscaler/pull/689

Initial hypotheses / findings:
- Autoscaler misconfiguration reduced headroom, enabling scale-down to a degree that left insufficient spare capacity when an unexpectedly heavy GPU consumer landed on shared nodes (classic noisy-neighbor).
- Noisy internal batch jobs were scheduled onto the same dedicated pool (scheduling policy allowed mixed workloads).
- GPU memory pressure and kernel pre-emption led to longer per-token latency and increased variance (p99).

Immediate mitigation performed:
- Reverted autoscaler scale-down aggressiveness to previous thresholds (rolled back PR) at 08:55 UTC.
- Temporarily increased pool target to 8 nodes and pinned customer-critical serving pods to isolated nodes where possible.
- Identified and evicted noisy internal job from the pool; moved it to a separate batch-only cluster.
- Enabled stricter admission control for long-running jobs in dedicated pools.

Follow-up actions / next steps:
- SRE to add autoscaler safe-guard: do not scale-down below N spare GPUs when committed dedicated pools have active customer traffic (action: SRE-1174).
- Platform to implement node taints/tolerations so customer-dedicated serving pods are not co-located with batch jobs by default (action: PLAT-2081).
- Runbook update: include checks for noisy-job detection and automated eviction triggers (action: SRE-1180).
- Customer compensation: one week of service credit agreed (handled by CS).

Customer communication summary sent to BrightWave at 2026-03-11 14:30 UTC: described root cause, mitigations applied, and planned fixes. Customer marked issue as acknowledged; follow-up review meeting scheduled for 2026-03-18.
